title: S040 5.5 Multiple Commands in Progress (Command Pipelining)
parent_path: S040 5.5 Multiple Commands in Progress (Command Pipelining)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY send another command without waiting for the completion result response of a command, subject to ambiguity rules and flow control constraints on the underlying data stream.
statements.trigger: client sends additional command without waiting for completion result

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY begin processing another command before processing the current command to completion, subject to ambiguity rules.
statements.trigger: server begins processing next command before current command completes

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Any command continuation request responses and command continuations MUST be negotiated before any subsequent command is initiated.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server detects a possible ambiguity, it MUST execute commands to completion in the order given by the client.
statements.trigger: ambiguity detected in pipelined command sequence
actions: execute commands to completion in order given by client

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client sends any command other than FETCH, STORE, or SEARCH, it MUST wait for the completion result response before sending a command with message sequence numbers.
statements.trigger: client sends command other than FETCH, STORE, or SEARCH
statements.pre_cond: command_type != FETCH & command_type != STORE & command_type != SEARCH
actions: wait for completion result response before sending command with message sequence numbers

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client sends a UID command, it MUST wait for a completion result response before sending a command that uses message sequence numbers.
actions: wait for completion result response before sending command with message sequence numbers

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers are prohibited from sending EXPUNGE responses while any of FETCH, STORE, or SEARCH commands are in progress.
statements.guard_semantics: EXPUNGE response prohibited when command_in_progress = FETCH | command_in_progress = STORE | command_in_progress = SEARCH
